title: Programming Languages and Frameworks
answer: The languages AI is written in and the frameworks built on top of them, tracked by adoption, releases, licence, and integrations.

reading.body:
The software layer of AI is tracked as three groups: 7 programming languages, 17 AI frameworks, and 12 inference engines.

The split matters because the three groups fail in different ways. Languages are few and change slowly, so a count of 7 is a stable base. Frameworks are the most crowded group at 17, which is where churn and consolidation happen. Inference engines sit at 12 and are the part closest to the hardware, since they determine how efficiently a model runs on a given accelerator.

For AI scaling, the inference layer is the one tied to compute and power. A serving engine that raises throughput per chip reduces how much new data centre capacity and electricity a workload needs. That makes this layer a partial substitute for building, though the data here records only that these engines exist and are tracked, not how much any of them improves efficiency.

What the data does not cover is adoption, releases, licence, or integrations, despite those being the stated dimensions. It gives counts and names only, with no dates, versions, or usage figures. Nothing here shows which language or framework is actually winning, or how any of it connects to the grid.
